sections.category: Apple rebuilds Siri at WWDC on a custom 1.2-trillion-parameter Google Gemini model, paying Google about $1 billion a year and conceding the assistant's core to a rival

bullets.body: At its WWDC keynote on Monday June 8 - Tim Cook's last as CEO - Apple unveiled a Siri rebuilt from the ground up and, in its most striking admission, said the new assistant is powered by a custom version of Google's Gemini rather than Apple's own models. The licensed model is a roughly 1.2-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts system, about eight times larger than the biggest cloud model Apple had built in-house, designated internally as "Apple Foundation Models v10"; the multi-year arrangement is reported to cost Apple on the order of $1 billion a year, with analyst estimates of total value up to $5 billion, per [9to5Mac - Apple nears $1 billion Google deal for custom Gemini model to power Siri](https://9to5mac.com/2025/11/05/google-gemini-1-billion-deal-apple-siri/) and [TechTimes - WWDC 2026: Gemini Powers Rebuilt Siri](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/317902/20260606/wwdc-2026-opens-monday-gemini-powers-rebuilt-siri-iphone-11-faces-ios-27-cut.htm). Apple's framing is that privacy is preserved by topology: a roughly 3-billion-parameter on-device model handles local requests, and anything heavier routes to Apple Silicon servers under Private Cloud Compute - stateless and ephemeral, with personally identifying information stripped before any content reaches the Gemini inference layer - rather than to Google's own infrastructure, per [Macworld - WWDC 2026 keynote announcements](https://www.macworld.com/article/678333/wwdc-keynote-event-time-what-launch-ios-macos-watchos-hardware.html). The user-visible result is a Siri that behaves like a full chatbot: a dedicated Siri app, a system-wide "Search or Ask" gesture, Dynamic Island integration, on-screen awareness, personal-context retrieval, and the ability to chain multi-step actions across apps; iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27, watchOS 27, tvOS 27 and visionOS 27 ship developer betas now, public betas in July, and a general release in the fall, per [Fast Company - What to expect from Apple at WWDC 26](https://www.fastcompany.com/91551472/apple-wwdc-26-when-what-to-expect-monday-siri-ai-gemini-ios-27-refined-liquid-glass-john-ternus). The significance is strategic, not cosmetic: after years of struggling to ship a competitive assistant, the iPhone maker has outsourced the intelligence layer of its flagship AI feature to the same company that pays it to be the default search engine - a bet that owning two billion devices and the user gateway matters more than owning the best model.

sections.category: WWDC opens Apple Intelligence to third-party assistants and deepens App Intents, turning the iPhone into a model-agnostic agent surface developers can target

bullets.body: The developer-facing half of Apple's WWDC announcement may matter more to the agent ecosystem than the Siri rebrand. iOS 27, iPadOS 27 and macOS 27 introduce an Extensions mechanism that lets users pick which assistant answers from the new "Search or Ask" panel - routing a query to Siri, Google Gemini, or ChatGPT, with Apple confirmed to have tested Anthropic's Claude as an additional option - which for the first time makes the system assistant a model-agnostic slot rather than a fixed Apple service, per [Gadgetbridge - Apple's WWDC 2026 kicks off today: Here is everything](https://www.gadgetbridge.com/news/apples-worldwide-developers-conference-wwdc-2026-kicks-off-today-here-is-everything/) and [TechTimes - WWDC 2026: Gemini Powers Rebuilt Siri](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/317902/20260606/wwdc-2026-opens-monday-gemini-powers-rebuilt-siri-iphone-11-faces-ios-27-cut.htm). Underneath, Apple is leaning on App Intents - the framework that lets Siri, Spotlight and Shortcuts invoke actions inside third-party apps - with a deeper integration that is the mechanism by which the new assistant chains tasks across apps, and on the Foundation Models framework that exposes the on-device model to developers for tool-calling and guided (structured) generation with no per-call charge, since the model runs locally, per [Computerworld - Why Apple's Foundation Models Framework matter](https://www.computerworld.com/article/4008276/why-apples-foundation-models-framework-matter.html). For anyone building agentic features, the practical takeaway is that the largest consumer device base is becoming an addressable agent surface in two directions at once: apps can expose their capabilities as intents an assistant can orchestrate, and apps can call a free on-device LLM for structured output and tool use - with the eventual assistant brain selectable by the user. The detailed API sessions run June 9-12, so the contours of how strict the entitlements and tool-permission model will be are still being filled in, but the direction - open the gateway, keep the platform - is now explicit.

sections.category: AI events to plan around now: WWDC is underway this week, with Databricks and the AI Engineer World's Fair next, plus the summer AI-security and AI-chip calendar

bullets.body: The still-upcoming AI calendar worth planning attendance around spans three tracks. On the mainstream developer side, Apple WWDC26 is underway now, having opened June 8 and running through June 12 with technical sessions on the new Siri and Foundation Models APIs, per [Gadgetbridge - Apple's WWDC 2026 kicks off today](https://www.gadgetbridge.com/news/apples-worldwide-developers-conference-wwdc-2026-kicks-off-today-here-is-everything/); the Databricks Data + AI Summit follows June 15-18 at Moscone (30,000-plus in person, 800-plus sessions); and the AI Engineer World's Fair runs June 28-July 2 at Moscone West with 29 tracks including multiple agentic and an inference and a security track, per [Moscone - AI Engineer World's Fair 2026](https://www.moscone.com/events/ai-engineer-worlds-fair-2026). On the AI-security track, the Confidential Computing Summit lands June 23-24 at the San Francisco Mint, with a schedule built around agent security, hardware-verified attestation and attested inference and speakers from NVIDIA, AMD, Google, Microsoft and Meta, per [PR Newswire - Confidential Computing Summit 2026 Schedule Showcases Next Era of AI Sovereignty](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/confidential-computing-summit-2026-schedule-showcases-next-era-of-ai-sovereignty-302765476.html); SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit follows August 11-12 at the Ritz-Carlton Half Moon Bay, per [SecurityWeek - AI Risk Summit 2026](https://www.airisksummit.com/); and in Las Vegas, Black Hat USA's AI Summit (single-day, August 4, inside the August 1-6 conference) and DEF CON 34's AI Village anchor the agentic red-teaming calendar, with OWASP Global AppSec USA in San Francisco November 2-6. Zenity - the practitioner-led AI Agent Security Summit the user tracks - has confirmed a 2026 global expansion to New York, London and APAC, with dates still worth monitoring. On the AI-chip and hardware track, AMD's Advancing AI 2026 event is slated for July, expected to detail availability for the Instinct MI400 / MI455X data-center GPU lineup unveiled at CES, per [AMD - AI Everywhere, for Everyone at CES 2026](https://www.amd.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026-1-5-amd-and-its-partners-share-their-vision-for-ai-ev.html); Hot Chips 2026 takes Stanford August 23-25, per [Hot Chips - HC38 (Aug 2026)](https://10times.com/hcs); and the AI Infra Summit runs September 15-17 at the Santa Clara Convention Center, per [AI Infra Summit 2026 - Venue](https://www.ai-infra-summit.com/venue). Further out, GitHub Universe returns to Fort Mason October 28-29 and AWS re:Invent runs November 30-December 4 in Las Vegas.
